facts.raw_span: 4 months of progressively worsening symmetric pain in the small joints of her hands, wrists, knees, and ankles
early morning stiffness lasting 2 hours daily
severe fatigue throughout the day
mild COVID-19 infection confirmed by SARS-CoV-2 PCR
denied fever, chills, night sweats, weight loss, rash, or appetite changes since recovering
erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 13 mm/hour
C-reactive protein of 4.3 mg/L
antinuclear antibody titer of 1:640
rheumatoid factor of 62.29 IU/mL
anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody of 237.39 units
MRI of the hands demonstrated synovitis of the bilateral distal radioulnar joints and the left second metacarpophalangeal joint
tenosynovitis around the extensor carpi ulnaris tendon

concepts.why: The patient presents with symmetric pain in the small joints, early morning stiffness, and severe fatigue, which are classic symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis, supported by high rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody levels.
The patient's recent history of COVID-19 infection and subsequent development of symmetric joint pain and synovitis suggests a possible diagnosis of reactive arthritis.
The patient's antinuclear antibody titer is elevated, and she presents with severe fatigue and joint pain, which could be indicative of systemic lupus erythematosus.
Although the patient denies a history of psoriasis, her joint pain and synovitis could be consistent with psoriatic arthritis, especially given the presence of tenosynovitis.
The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not fit neatly into one specific autoimmune disease, suggesting a possible diagnosis of undifferentiated connective tissue disease.
The patient's joint pain, synovitis, and tenosynovitis are consistent with inflammatory arthritis, although the specific subtype is unclear.
The patient's recent history of COVID-19 infection and subsequent development of joint pain and synovitis suggests a possible diagnosis of post-infectious arthritis.
The patient's joint pain and synovitis, in the absence of rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, could be consistent with seronegative arthritis.

rationales.F01: Symmetric small joint pain is characteristic of Rheumatoid Arthritis.
rationales.F02: Early morning stiffness is a common symptom of Rheumatoid Arthritis and Inflammatory Arthritis.
rationales.F04: Recent infection can trigger Reactive Arthritis or Post-infectious Arthritis.
rationales.F08: High antinuclear antibody titer can be seen in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Undifferentiated Connective Tissue Disease.
rationales.F09: Elevated rheumatoid factor is often found in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
rationales.F10: Presence of anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody is highly specific for Rheumatoid Arthritis and helps rule out other types of arthritis.
